To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MODIS ACAOD retrievals are in excellent agreement with the direct airborne measurements made by NASA’s AATS and 5STAR sensors, and (2) the MODIS color ratio method is an effective tool to retrieve ACAOD over the low-level cloud decks.

the MODIS above-cloud aerosol retrieval algorithm performs reasonably well in retrieving the aerosol optical depth over low level clouds, with an average bias of 0.05 and an average RMSE of 0.16, when the algorithm is applied to the MODIS Level-1B reflectance product (MOD03), and the MODIS Level 1A radiance product (MOD021KM), respectively.

the MODIS ACAOD retrievals are validated by the airborne measurements made by the AATS and 5STAR sensors and the results of this validation study are consistent with previous studies that used different methods to retrieve ACAOD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of the MODIS above-cloud aerosol products.
the retrieval of the ACAOD over the global oceans from the MODIS data using a new method.
the validation of MODIS ACAOD products retrieved from the “Color Ratio” method applied to the satellite measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the above-cloud aerosol retrieval from the MODIS color ratio algorithm is validated using direct measurements made by AATS and 3STAR sensors.
the MODIS ACAOD retrievals are reliable for partially absorbing aerosols and the color ratio algorithm is robust and applicable to the MODIS measurements.
the MODIS ACAOD product, when compared with the limited number of direct measurements, has a high potential to retrieve ACAOD with reasonable accuracy and precision over land.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MODIS ACAOD retrievals from the “color-ratio” algorithm are reliable and robust for partially absorbing aerosols, but not for highly absorbing ones such as black carbon.

the color ratio method applied to the MODIS cloudy-scan reflectance measurements is capable of retrieving above-cloud aerosol information, but the accuracy of the retrieval depends on the type of absorbing aerosols and their optical properties, as well as the cloud properties.

the MODIS ACAOD retrieval algorithm has the capability to retrieve the ACAOD with an uncertainty of 0.05-0.1, which is comparable with the current uncertainty of MODIS aerosol optical depth retrieval over land.
The main takeaway from our work is that

MODIS ACAOD retrievals are consistent with airborne measurements and the color ratio method can be applied with confidence for the global analysis of the spatial and temporal variability of the ACAOD.
the MODIS ACAOD retrievals are reliable for partially absorbing aerosols and can provide valuable data for aerosol radiative forcing estimation, air quality modeling, and climate modeling studies.
the color ratio method is able to retrieve above-cloud aerosol properties with reasonable accuracy and precision, and it is capable of capturing the variability of above-cloud aerosols.
